driver: user, exercising an interactive assistant in the local stack
summary: Defects found by driving the feature by hand, after Phases 6-8 had signed off. Each was reproduced from the live log or the stored surface before any change, and each fix carries a test that failed first. Two classes emerged: our own defects, and model-authoring failures that the feature handled badly.

our_defects.found_as: the model produced legacy-protocol components ({"type": "textinput"}) and every surface was rejected
our_defects.root_cause: render_prompt_section called the SDK's generate_system_prompt with role_description only. include_schema defaults to False, so the prompt carried NO component schemas at all — 1152 characters describing components abstractly — and additionally instructed the model to emit <a2ui-json> blocks in its reply, a transport this backend does not use.
our_defects.fix: Assemble the section from catalog_description(include_schema=True) plus our transport text. 733 -> 40427 characters, with the component discriminator and every component schema present.
our_defects.test_that_would_have_caught_it: the existing test asserted `'a2ui-json' in section` — it pinned the wrong transport and never checked that the catalog was there at all

our_defects.found_as: the model kept inventing option properties (`disabled`, then `description`) even with the full schemas in the prompt
our_defects.root_cause: A2UI's own tool-based integration (a2ui.adk.send_a2ui_to_client_toolset) keeps the schema in the system instructions and binds the tool to it through the tool description, which names the delimiters the SDK emits. Our prompt carried those delimiters, but the tool description pointed at a '## Interactive user input' section that does not exist anywhere in the rendered prompt. The one link the design rests on was broken.
our_defects.fix: Point the argument description at ---BEGIN/END A2UI JSON SCHEMA---, state that objects there are closed, and add a test asserting the named block is really present.

our_defects.found_as: 422 'Field inputNumber must be a string' on a form the user had filled in correctly
our_defects.root_cause: The renderer writes a real number for a TextField of variant number (deliberate: numeric checks otherwise compare against a string), while intake required a string from every TextField.
our_defects.fix: Accept int/float for the number variant, excluding bool (an int subclass in Python, so a checkbox answer would have passed as a number).

our_defects.found_as: a form arrived with no submit button
our_defects.root_cause: The model emitted the Button but no container referenced it. An orphan component is legal A2UI — the validator only rejects the opposite, a reference to a missing component — and our answerability check tested for presence, not reachability.
our_defects.fix: Require a Button with an action event reachable from 'root' (walking children/child/content/trigger/tabs), excluding Modal triggers, whose click opens the dialog instead of submitting.

our_defects.found_as: clicking a button that should open a modal submitted the form instead
our_defects.root_cause: ModalRenderer attached opening to a wrapper around the trigger while the trigger Button kept its own action, so a click did both — and the submit ends the turn, so the dialog was never seen. The SDK's reference Modal has the same gap.
our_defects.fix: Give the trigger subtree a context that makes the control open the dialog instead of dispatching; content buttons still submit.

our_defects.found_as: fields that should be optional behaved as mandatory
our_defects.root_cause: An empty text binding held no value at all. Checks run against the data model and the SDK's regex function calls test(value), where an absent value stringifies to "undefined" — so an author's pattern written to allow empty (^$|...) could never match, and the field reported an error the user could not clear.
our_defects.fix: Text and date inputs seed "" when their binding has no value (the Slider precedent); the number variant is excluded, where empty means no number yet.

our_defects.found_as: a broken image, then a silently dead video player
our_defects.root_cause: Media had no failure state. Agent-authored URLs are frequently wrong — an invented 404, and a YouTube watch page that a plain <video> can never play.
our_defects.fix: Degrade to the media placeholder on load error, for image, video and audio.

our_defects.found_as: the validation error read as a wire-format problem ('deleteSurface' is a required property)
our_defects.root_cause: A wire message is a oneOf over four message types, so one bad component makes jsonschema report every branch it tried. The actionable line was buried among branches that were never in play — and the model reads this text on its next turn.
our_defects.fix: Filter the structured error details by path, name the failing component, and list the properties the catalog does not define for it (resolved from the catalog, including nested objects such as an option).

our_defects.found_as: the user asked whether the two halves disagree about the contract
our_defects.root_cause: The BE<->FE contract test compared component NAMES only, while the two halves reach the catalog through independently versioned packages. A property known only to the backend would be advertised to the model and silently ignored by the renderer.
our_defects.fix: The frontend manifest now publishes the properties of each component and the backend test compares them one by one. Full diff of the 18 components: one difference, List.listStyle, frontend-only (the inert direction).

our_defects.found_as: the prompt had accumulated hand-written rules about components
our_defects.root_cause: Each model failure was answered by adding prose to the prompt (action is a oneOf, checks hold validation, objects are closed, there is no 'disabled' option). That is a second, hand-maintained spec of the catalog which can drift from the catalog the renderer and validator use — the cost this migration exists to remove. Recorded as a defect on the user's explicit constraint.
our_defects.fix: Remove every authored component rule. A test now decomposes the rendered section into role text, transport text, the catalog-valid example and the SDK's catalog description, and fails if a single character comes from anywhere else.

model_authoring_failures_handled.observed: a bare id string in the components list, immediately before the object it names (twice)
model_authoring_failures_handled.handling: Dropped during argument parsing when it duplicates a declared component: it carries no meaning there, and rejecting it cost the user a turn before the tool could report anything. A string naming no declared component still fails.

model_authoring_failures_handled.observed: properties the Basic Catalog does not define — `disabled` and `description` on ChoicePicker options. The assistant's own instructions demanded them verbatim: "Starter excludes SSO, Audit log, On-premise and Critical support — show them disabled with the reason". The model was obeying its prompt, not improvising.
model_authoring_failures_handled.handling: Dropped, with the surface still emitted. Product decision after two reversals: losing the whole form is not an acceptable outcome, because the user gets nothing while the fields and the submit control were expressible all along. What reaches the client is exactly the catalog's vocabulary — conformance, not repair — and the gating the instructions asked for could never have been performed by a Basic Catalog surface in any case. Dropped paths are logged; the answer is validated against the declared options, so nothing is loosened server-side. A component the catalog lacks is still refused.

known_gaps_recorded: A rejected surface ends the turn: create_react_agent captures the NAMES of return_direct tools when the graph is built, so the model cannot correct itself within the same turn. The tool streams a plain-text notice, but that notice is not persisted — the assistant message is rebuilt from AI messages only, so a reloaded conversation shows an empty turn.

GenerationResult already carries tool_errors to the client and the frontend ignores the field entirely. Surfacing it would make every tool failure legible instead of empty, but it changes platform behaviour for all return_direct tools, so it awaits a product decision.
An argument-parsing failure happens before the tool runs, so even the notice cannot fire there.

The Sales Proposal assistant is written against form capabilities this feature does not have: disabled options, a field whose requiredness depends on another field's value, and re-rendering the same form with errors. Surfaces are static and turn-based — emitted once, ending the turn. Its instructions need rewriting to what the catalog expresses, which is also the honest test of the feature.
